These are requirements and recommendations for the addition extending version 2, not approval of future bytes.

Necessary content and placement

Place a clearly headed 'Practice summary' section inside the feedback after the explanatory review. Generate it automatically for each nonempty submission; neither copying nor completing a reflection is required. Keep a short submission label visible, such as 'Last submitted response — submission 2 in this applied case — changed wording'. Describe changes as submission events using the assessment colleague's language, without implying improvement or that self-review occurred.

Use short plain-text headings to separate the practice label, submission event, applied scenario, learner's submitted response, feedback and one next practice action. Preserve the applied title, all facts, all operating conditions and the task. Preserve the submitted response verbatim, including its line breaks. Use a distinct 'Learner's submitted response' heading so that it cannot be confused with the tool's guidance or an editable draft. Reuse the feedback actually offered, including its interpretation limits, rather than add another explanation with a different meaning. The copy must stand alone with 'PRACTICE SUMMARY — fictional exercise; not a verified workplace outcome.'

Concision should come from compact headings and avoiding extra commentary. Do not shorten the record by omitting a qualification, cutting off a response, or replacing the operating conditions with the scenario title. User-supplied cases and responses can make the complete summary longer. The one next action can be the assessment colleague's invitation: 'Check one part of your submitted response against the applied facts and operating conditions, revising or keeping the wording as warranted.' This connects the record to a useful optional review operation without adding a second assignment or requiring a change.

Copying and navigation

Provide the complete plain text in a clearly labeled, read-only area that learners can reach, select and copy with a keyboard. It should wrap on a narrow screen, preserve visible section boundaries and allow access to all of its content. Copying must be optional and must not submit a response, change the draft, reset the practice or initiate sharing. A successful copy should have a brief confirmation; if a copy shortcut is unavailable, retain the text and give a clear manual selection-and-copy route. Software Engineering should choose and verify the technical mechanism, including offline behavior. No identity field or additional personal information is needed.

Make the route back to the editable response easy to find from feedback. Returning to revision must preserve any draft already being edited, keep the case and review available, and identify the retained summary as the last submitted attempt. Copying during revision copies that submitted record, not the current draft. A nearby sentence can say, 'Edits are not included until you try the response again.' The learner may revise, retain warranted wording or leave; no compulsory copy or reflection step should interrupt those choices.

State changes the learner must understand

A later nonempty submission replaces the current summary with a record of that submission, whether the wording changed or stayed the same. A blank submission creates no new summary: explain that no new response was submitted, and label any retained record as the last submitted attempt. Pending scenario edits do not alter the summary's case. Successful application of a scenario starts a fresh practice and clears the preceding summary; invalid application retains the applied case and its existing practice record while the error can be corrected. Skip clears the draft, review and summary without producing a substitute performance record, and voluntary return starts fresh. Reset clears the current practice and summary and restores the starting case as already described. Update the existing action help to include the summary in these clearing consequences; describe clearing this page's practice, without promising deletion of copies elsewhere.

Optional refinements and focused verification

To reduce the repeated reading identified in m00026, the complete summary text may sit in an optional disclosure within feedback, with its heading, submission label and route to the text always visible. A dedicated 'Copy practice summary' button is a convenience; the keyboard-selectable plain-text route remains necessary. Placing a return-to-draft action at the end of feedback and changing 'beside this draft' to 'shown on this page' remain useful refinements for narrow screens. These refinements do not require another practice stage or an attempt-history display.

Software Engineering should directly address the same-submission association identified in m00059 and verify that the summary, copy result, retained draft and clearing behavior match these learner-facing descriptions. Targeted checks should include copying while a draft differs from the last submission, a changed and an unchanged resubmission, blank input, pending and invalid scenario edits, successful scenario application, skip and reset. Also check that a learner can find the summary, access all its text and return to the draft using a keyboard and a narrow display. Those checks have not occurred for this feature; this response claims no accessibility certification, measured reading burden, human completion time, learning result or new domain approval.

response.content:
I approve implemented artifact version 3 within assessment and evaluation design, specifically the practice-summary content, its association with the submitted response and offered guidance, and the event descriptions and inference limits requested in m00068. This is a review of the supplied implementation, using my proposal in m00059. It is not execution verification or evidence of a human outcome. I find no necessary assessment correction in this addition.

Standalone content and meaning

The implemented summary begins with 'PRACTICE SUMMARY — fictional exercise; not a verified workplace outcome.' It includes the applied scenario title, every supplied fact, every operating condition and the task. Its construction does not shorten these fields to a title or remove qualifications. The learner's submitted field value appears under its own verbatim-response heading, without correction, paraphrase or a favorable interpretation. These distinctions preserve the evidence needed to reconsider what the response claims, including when changed conditions make a previously plausible action inappropriate. Compact headings provide organization; long supplied content can still produce a long summary without being truncated.

The feedback heading explicitly identifies general self-review guidance rather than an assessment of this response. The visible review and copied feedback use the same guidance strings. Both retain the four relevant questions: trace an observation to its supporting fact and material limits; distinguish established evidence from an explanation requiring confirmation; identify what clarification could reveal and how it could change the next decision; and examine the prerequisites for a proposed action. The guidance permits an explanation supported by changed facts instead of treating every explanation as automatically unsupported. It also preserves the warning that these prompts may not fit an edited task with another purpose.

The copied guidance states that the tool has not determined whether the observation is supported, the question useful or the action feasible. It identifies the prompts as general guidance, says that punctuation, phrases and keywords do not judge the response, and disclaims improvement, learning, transfer and workplace competence from submission or revision. The summary therefore does not present an independent rating or endorse the learner's proposed workplace action. A claim made inside the learner's response remains the learner's submitted wording, not a tool finding. The record shows guidance offered; it does not show that the learner read, understood or applied it.

The implemented next practice action is the invitation proposed in m00059: 'Check one part of your submitted response against the applied facts and operating conditions, revising or keeping the wording as warranted.' It asks for examination of the practice response, permits keeping justified wording and neither assumes an error nor directs execution of the proposed workplace action. It is an invitation, not a statement that review has occurred.

Submission events

The initial event reads 'Initial response submitted.' Changed wording receives 'Changed response submitted; improvement not assessed.' Identical wording receives 'Unchanged response submitted. No correctness or improvement judgment was made.' These descriptions distinguish observable submission events without inferring a reasoning process. In particular, version 3 preserves the correction that resolved m00024: repeated wording is not described as occurring after self-review. A considered decision to retain wording and repeated activation without reviewing remain alternative explanations compatible with that event. Submission numbering identifies sequence within the applied case; it supplies neither a capability score nor a learner identity.

The blank-response wording says that no new response was submitted and, when a prior record exists, explicitly identifies the retained review and summary as belonging to the last submitted attempt. It does not represent a blank draft as a completed or failed assessment. The skipped-state wording similarly makes no capability judgment and describes the practice record as cleared. Voluntary return is represented as fresh practice, without a summary suggesting that the skip produced performance evidence.

Same-submission association

Software Engineering's direct answer in m00065 addresses the concern I raised in m00059. The supplied implementation represents the applied scenario, exact submitted response, event and guidance together in one saved submission record. The summary is constructed from that record, and the visible review uses that record's guidance. The summary display uses the saved summary rather than the current response draft or unapplied scenario-editor text. This addresses the assessment-content requirement that the evidence context, response and offered feedback belong to the same submission.

The accompanying labels identify the last submitted attempt and explain that later edits are excluded until another submission. The supplied transitions represent a subsequent nonempty submission as replacing the record, a blank submission as retaining the prior record without incrementing it, an invalid scenario application as preserving the existing applied context, and successful application as starting a fresh practice. Skip, reset and voluntary return are represented as clearing the prior summary. The clearing descriptions appropriately distinguish this page from copies made elsewhere. These findings accept the supplied design and content association; they do not certify that those transitions or copying work in a browser.

Evidence boundary

The addition remains a record of supported practice. A response that changes after guidance could reflect the cues, additional time or familiarity with the case. An independent assessment would require a separately collected first response to a reviewed changed task, with relevant case evidence available and without a worked response or component-by-component guidance before that attempt. The summary itself supplies no such evidence, no retention measure and no causal estimate of learning. No additional mandatory learner task is needed for this summary request.

Version 3's focused execution checks remain outstanding, including whether the copied record stays associated correctly during draft edits, pending or invalid scenario edits, repeated and blank submissions, and clearing transitions. Version 2 observations cannot establish those results for the addition. Learning Experience Design's review of the journey, and the appropriate colleagues' verification of keyboard, selection, copying, narrow-screen and offline behavior, remain separate. This message records assessment-domain approval of version 3's implemented content and interpretation boundaries only; it does not record readiness, a freeze, test success or demonstrated learning.

I approve implemented version 3 within learning-experience design for the practice-summary addition: its placement in the existing journey, distinction between submitted wording and an editable draft, optional access and copying route, return navigation, and explained practice-state consequences. This is a review of the supplied implementation against my criteria in m00061, responding to m00068 and Software Engineering's account in m00065. I find no necessary learning-experience correction before focused testing. This approval does not establish that selection, copying, keyboard navigation or narrow-screen operation works in a browser.

Placement and purpose

The learner still makes a meaningful attempt by composing a response to the applied fictional case, then receives explanatory self-review with optional revision. Version 3 places a clearly headed Practice summary section inside Practice review, after the explanatory guidance. A nonempty submission supplies the record automatically; copying and completing the optional reflection are not prerequisites for returning to the response or leaving. The addition therefore provides a record of the existing practice without creating another required task.

After submission, the summary heading, last-submission label, explanatory note and Open plain-text practice summary control remain outside the collapsed text area. This makes the record's existence and purpose discoverable without requiring another immediate reading of the complete case and feedback. The full text is available through that disclosure under the label Complete plain-text summary for the last submitted attempt. Its headings distinguish the applied scenario, facts, operating conditions, task, learner's submitted response, offered guidance and next practice action. The supplied construction retains the complete fields and response rather than shortening them to a title or excerpt. The read-only presentation distinguishes this record from the response field where changes belong. These are appropriate content-organization choices; whether learners find and read the complete text comfortably remains unobserved.

The record's next action asks the learner to check one part of the submitted response against the applied facts and conditions, revising or keeping wording as warranted. Within the activity, that offers a manageable way back into review while preserving the choice to retain a supported response. It does not require copying, a cosmetic edit or an additional reflection. The explanatory review continues to offer concrete operations with the learner's own wording: consult supporting evidence, retain uncertainty, identify what clarification could change, and examine a proposed step's conditions. Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation's separate version 3 approval in m00070 addresses the interpretation boundaries of this content; I am approving its role and organization in the learning journey.

Submitted record and current draft

The visible label identifies the last submitted response, its submission number within the applied case and whether the wording is initial, changed or unchanged. The adjacent note explicitly says that edits are excluded until the response is tried again and that pending scenario edits do not change the record. The review itself also identifies its connection to the last submitted response. This repeated distinction is useful at the two locations where a learner could otherwise mistake retained feedback or copied text for a review of current edits.

Software Engineering's supplied implementation and direct explanation in m00065 address the experience requirement that copying during revision refers to the submitted attempt. The represented summary uses the saved submission record, while Return to draft and Revise response return attention to the existing editable response without replacing it. The status text explains that another submission updates the review and summary. I accept that represented association and navigation design; execution must still establish that the retained draft and copied text behave accordingly.

The return-to-draft action at the end of feedback implements the refinement proposed in m00026 and m00061. It gives a clear route back after the explanatory review, optional summary and reflection. The response help now refers to the applied case shown on this page, which also removes the earlier layout-dependent wording. These changes improve the represented route between case, attempt and review without adding a mandatory stage.

Optional selection and copying

The copying instructions describe both keyboard commands and a device's own selection and Copy commands. Select summary text accurately names the convenience control: its accompanying help and selection-status wording distinguish selecting text from actually copying it. The fallback asks the learner to select manually and use the device's Copy command. No displayed message claims that a copy has succeeded merely because selection was established. A separate direct-copy button was optional in m00061; this labeled native route meets the proposed interaction design without it.

The summary remains available as complete plain text, and copying is expressly optional. Selecting the record is represented as separate from submitting, changing the draft, clearing practice or sharing. A read-only, scrollable text area with wrapping is a reasonable implementation of the requested access route, subject to the outstanding checks. I cannot certify its actual selection behavior, assistive-technology experience, clipping or reachability on a phone from the supplied source.

Understandable state changes

Another nonempty submission replaces the current record, with neutral initial, changed or unchanged event wording. A blank draft creates no new record, and its error and status text explicitly identify any retained review and summary as belonging to the last submitted attempt. The learner is therefore told why older content remains available after a blank activation instead of being given a misleading completion message.

Pending scenario edits are labeled unapplied. Invalid application gives a recoverable error and says that the applied case, current practice and last submitted summary remain unchanged. Successful application is described beforehand as starting fresh and clearing the preceding response, reflection, review and summary. The represented distinction allows users to correct editor mistakes while keeping the current practice understandable, and makes a successfully changed situation a fresh attempt on its new evidence.

Skip explains its clearing consequences before activation and leaves a voluntary Return to this case route with a fresh draft. That return after skipping is distinct from Return to draft during revision: the former starts fresh, while the latter preserves the current work and last submitted record. Reset explains that it also discards pending scenario edits and restores the starting fictional case. The revised help consistently limits clearing to this page and acknowledges that copies made elsewhere remain. These explanations match the intended choices without promising recovery of cleared work or deletion of an external copy.

Remaining evidence and scope

Software Engineering should verify these represented requirements in the focused version 3 tests: access and selection of the complete summary; copying while the draft differs from the last submission; draft-preserving return; changed, unchanged and blank resubmissions; pending and invalid scenario edits; valid application; skip, voluntary return and reset. Keyboard and narrow-screen checks should establish that the summary can be found, its entire text reached and the editable draft revisited. Selection feedback must be inspected separately from the actual copied content. These are outstanding verification requirements, not observed results.

The optional disclosure addresses the identified risk of repeated reading through organization, but actual reading burden, completion time and learner understanding remain unknown. No human observation establishes that someone distinguishes the record from the draft or uses the next action productively. Version 2 observations cannot verify the version 3 addition, and this message does not extend another specialist's approval. My approval is confined to the implemented learning-experience decisions described above; it is not a readiness message, runtime freeze, technical certification or claim of learning.

Temporary coverage requires an available incoming teammate to agree; no such agreement is supplied in this case.

evidence_refs.quote: This is a capability to reason from evidence under changing conditions, not to reproduce one preferred sentence.

Each prompt has a learning purpose: tracing a statement to a fact exposes an unsupported inference; connecting a question to a decision distinguishes useful clarification from a question included merely to satisfy the task; checking conditions makes feasibility part of the reasoning.

A material limitation remains: a learner may lack the understanding needed to recognize a problem in their own response, and these general prompts do not establish that such a misunderstanding was corrected.

Proposed evidence that could challenge a learning claim: learners improve the prompted revision yet continue to assert unsupported explanations on a new case; reproduce the seed's action when changed constraints make it infeasible; or ask a question whose answer cannot inform their proposed next step.

An independent assessment would require a separately collected first response to a reviewed changed task, with relevant case evidence available and without a worked response or component-by-component guidance before that attempt.
